lines: The testament testamentar and Inventar
of the guidis geir debtis and sowmes of money qlkis
pertenit to umqle Niniane glasgow fischer burges
of glasgow the tyme of his deceiss Quha deceist in
the moneth of Januar [1613]
[inventory and incoming debts partly unresolved]
At glasgow the [day unresolved] day of Januar 1613 zeiris
The qlk day Niniane glasgow seik in bodie
And of perfyt memorie [commends] his saull to god and his bodie to be bureit
Item he nominat and constitut Jonet hutchesoun his spous & Robert
glasgow his sone his onlie ex[ecutouris]
[Lower bequest/support wording, including a possible William name, is physically lost and cannot be restored]
and sustein him for the present [term unresolved] and na langer
Item to Johne glasgw his brother [amount/clothing wording unresolved]
Item to Marioun glasgw his sister ten merkis
Item to Elizabet hutchesoun [legacy amount unresolved]
Item to Robert glasgw his sone ane hundreth pundis money
[residue, witnesses and confirmation partly unresolved]
[administrative continuation naming the estate of Ninian Glasgow]
the saidis Jonet hutchesoun & Robert glasgow [continuation unresolved]
[caution and closing formula unresolved]
[following estate excluded]

plain_english: Ninian Glasgow was a fisher and burgess of Glasgow who died in January 1613.
Jonet Hutchesoun is expressly his spouse and Robert Glasgow expressly his son; both are named as his only executors. The kin terms, not executorship, prove those two relationships.
John Glasgow is expressly Ninian's brother and Marioun Glasgow expressly his sister. Robert is again called son and left one hundred pounds.

The damaged lower edge contains a possible William name followed by continuation wording about sustaining him, but the missing leaf prevents recovery of the relationship. It cannot make William another son.
Elizabeth Hutchesoun receives a legacy without a stated relationship. Witness and caution names remain too incomplete to support additional family reconstruction.
findings: Confirmed: fisher, burgess of Glasgow and death in January 1613.
Confirmed: Jonet Hutchesoun spouse and Robert Glasgow son; both only executors.
Confirmed: John Glasgow brother, Marioun Glasgow sister and Robert Glasgow son in parallel legacy clauses.
Confirmed: Marioun's legacy is ten merks and Robert's is one hundred pounds.
Unresolved after direct edge-to-continuation reread: William's name/role and the person to be sustained cannot be linked securely because the decisive words are physically missing.
Confirmed: Elizabeth Hutchesoun is a legatee only; no kin term is visible.
Excluded: the record does not identify brother John as Glasgow-1030.
changes_from_previous: Old: the damaged William/support clause was unresolved. New: inspection across the torn edge and next-page continuation confirms the loss is physical; no relationship can responsibly be recovered.
Old: spouse, son, brother and sister readings were maintained. New: all four are confirmed unchanged from the ink.
Old: Elizabeth Hutchesoun's relationship was unstated. New: confirmed unchanged; legacy does not establish kinship.
No walkthrough text or geometry changed because the damaged-William conclusion remains the same.
unresolved: William's complete name, bequest/support role and relationship, if any.
Identity of brother John and whether the siblings were full or half siblings.
Several account parties, witness names, exact testament day and confirmation/caution formula.
profiles: John Glasgow: excluded as a proved identity for the brother
William Glasgow: possible name in damaged passage, no proved relationship
confidence_statement: High for occupation, spouse, son, brother, sister and stated legacies. High that the damaged text cannot establish William as a child. Low for William's role, several account/witness names and administrative wording. No relationship is inferred from executorship, legacy or surname alone.
